message.content:
**Order filled:** bought 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 limit — $9,812 total, within the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, with no funds moved out of the account.

**Summary:** I read Apple's fiscal 2024 Form 10-K (filed 2024-11-01) and its Q4 press release, and checked the latest news and quotes. The fundamentals support a modest buy: fiscal 2024 net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, and operating income grew to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion, driven by Services (+13% to $96.2 billion). Net income was **$93,736 million in fiscal 2024** versus **$96,995 million in fiscal 2023** — the decline is entirely explained by the one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge from the European Commission's State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), not by operating deterioration; pre-tax income actually rose to $123.5 billion from $113.7 billion, and operating cash flow was a strong $118.3 billion. News flow was neutral-to-constructive — iPhone 16 supplier builds described as "steady into December," holiday-quarter estimates unchanged, and shares "little changed" around $222 as investors weigh iPhone 16 demand and the Apple Intelligence rollout — so there was no negative catalyst to override the operating trend. With the stock at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $223.00, a limit essentially at the market, which filled at $223.00 for roughly $9,812 — comfortably inside the mandate's per-order and daily limits, and leaving the $50,000 cash balance otherwise intact.
